name: Thin Section
desc: A petrographic thin section under crossed polars — a mosaic of interlocking mineral grains blazing in Michel-Levy interference colours, each grain swinging through its own extinction as the microscope stage turns slowly, twinned feldspars ruled with fine lamellae and micas split along cleavage.

grains.doc: number of mineral grains across the field — few big crystals to a fine-grained mosaic

energy.doc: interference brightness and saturation, plus the sub-stage sheen

scale.doc: magnification — zoom into the grain mosaic

hue.doc: base tint bias (crossed colours are physical; shifts plane/sketch mineral colours)

speed.doc: how fast the microscope stage rotates and the light pool drifts

x.doc: azimuth of the drifting sub-stage illumination pool

y.doc: vertical bias of the illumination (reserved anchor)

style.doc: crossed_polars: physical birefringence — jewel interference colours with extinction as the stage turns · plane_polarized: single polariser, natural mineral body colours, relief and pleochroism · false_color: EBSD-style orientation map, each grain a flat hue · sketch: petrographic ink drawing on a toned plate, grain boundaries inked, extinction as tone

seed.doc: a fresh rock — new grain shapes, orientations, mineralogy and twinning
